title: Fine-grained heterogeneous change detection in complex disaster response with wavelet-based spatial-frequency coupled learning
abstract: Heterogeneous remote sensing change detection (CD) based on optical and SAR imagery is essential for rapid disaster monitoring, as it overcomes single-sensor limitations and enables all-weather observation. However, the inherent heterogeneity between optical and SAR modalities—stemming from their disparate imaging mechanisms—results in poor feature comparability, significantly impeding fine-grained, accurate change identification. To address the issue, this study explores a combination of data-level strategies and methodological enhancements. First, to alleviate the data scarcity, this study constructs two sub-meter (0.35 m) heterogeneous datasets tailored for earthquake building damage and flood assessment, thereby providing a high-resolution data foundation for fine-grained disaster monitoring. Second, a Siamese Spatial–Frequency Coupled Network (SSFCNet) is introduced to mitigate the cross-modal discrepancy. Specifically, a Spatial-Frequency Coupled Encoder (SFCE) is designed to simultaneously model spatial semantics and frequency directional features via wavelet transforms, thereby aligning heterogeneous representations while mitigating noise. To refine change representation, an Explicit Change Guidance Module (ECGM) is designed to incorporate distinct difference priors into the decoding stage. Subsequently, a Multi-scale Inverse Wavelet Decoder (MIWD) exploits the invertibility of wavelet transforms to restore high-frequency details, preventing information loss during upsampling. Finally, a Boundary-Aware Loss (BAL) is devised to enforce geometric consistency along change boundaries through gradient constraints. Extensive experiments on five public datasets and the two newly constructed datasets demonstrate that SSFCNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of detection accuracy and boundary integrity. Notably, the proposed method achieves an optimal balance between performance and computational efficiency, demonstrating its potential for rapid, robust emergency response. For reproducibility, our code and data are available at https://github.com/yangyang12318/SSFCNet.
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: FreqChange: Frequency-aware spatiotemporal learning with prior guidance for semantic change detection in remote sensing images
abstract: Semantic change detection plays a critical role in monitoring Earth’s surface dynamics by identifying the locations and semantic categories of changes from bi-temporal remote sensing images. Existing methods primarily employ a shared-weight image encoder coupled with a change extractor to detect changes in the spatial domain, while lacking sufficient temporal modeling and effective exploitation of semantic priors. As a result, they struggle to accurately localize changed regions and maintain intra-class semantic consistency. To address these limitations, we propose FreqChange, a frequency-aware spatiotemporal learning framework with semantic prior guidance. Specifically, a frequency change-aware module (FCAM) is integrated into the spatiotemporal learning framework to accurately perceive and localize changed regions by comprehensively analyzing both low- and high-frequency components between bi-temporal features. Additionally, to enhance the intra-class semantic consistency of bi-temporal images, we propose a semantic consistency enhancement module (SCEM), which leverages semantic priors derived from large-scale pre-trained vision foundation models, combined with semantic consistency upsampling, to effectively facilitate spatiotemporal learning. Through their collaborative integration, these modules collectively enable the precise detection of land cover changes from bi-temporal images while preserving intra-class semantic consistency. Extensive experiments on four well-recognized datasets (i.e., HRSCD, SECOND, HiUCD-mini, and Landsat-SCD) demonstrate that FreqChange consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative metrics and qualitative visualizations. By uniting frequency-domain analysis and semantic priors, FreqChange establishes a new paradigm for accurate and reliable semantic change detection in remote sensing.

title: MiMNet-STASF: a spatiotemporal decoupled network for sub-pixel canopy structure retrieval of urban forests with multi-source long-term remote sensing time series
abstract: Forest canopy height (FCH) and vertical structural composition are essential for urban ecological assessment and precision forest management, yet reliable retrieval in fragmented urban–rural transition landscapes remains challenging due to multi-source sensor heterogeneity, seasonal dynamics, and mixed canopy conditions within 10 m pixels. We propose MiMNet-STASF, a spatiotemporal fusion framework for grid-level canopy-structure inversion from 24-month Sentinel-1/2 time series. The framework integrates a nested Mamba architecture (Inner VMamba for multi-scale spatial encoding and Outer bidirectional Mamba for long-range temporal dependency modeling), an adaptive Spatiotemporal Arbiter Gated Fusion (STASF) module (SG/TG/STAG), and a physics-informed hierarchical regression head that jointly estimates FCH and vertical structural fractions (<10 m, 10–20 m, and ≥20 m). Using UAV LiDAR-derived supervision, validated in Xiong’an New Area against 13 deep learning models spanning four architectural paradigms (RNNs, CNNs, Transformers, SSMs), MiMNet-STASF outperforms all comparatives, achieving an R2 of 0.8963 and an RMSE of 1.0903 m for FCH retrieval. Ablation results indicate that the nested Mamba and STASF components provide clearer gains on structurally imbalanced targets. From a data perspective, Sentinel-1 provides enhanced structural sensitivity, Sentinel-2 offers stable spectral and phenological context, and vegetation indices (VI) further improve vegetation contrast; their fusion enhances prediction consistency across canopy-height gradients and vertical fractional components. Moreover, MiMNet-STASF retains robust structural representations under seasonal vegetation variation. Together with cross-regional GEDI-referenced evaluation, these results support MiMNet-STASF as an effective and scalable solution for management-oriented, fine-grained urban forest canopy-structure mapping. The implementation of the proposed method is publicly available at https://github.com/qinjs123/MiMNet-STASF.

title: DCMArb: Decoupled-Collaborative Mamba for Arbitrary-scale Hyperspectral Super-resolution
abstract: Hyperspectral imagery (HSI) super-resolution (SR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. However, existing methods typically apply homogeneous processing to spatial-spectral features, leading to heterogeneity conflicts at the physical level. Specifically, the spatial dimension primarily exhibits locally continuous long-range dependencies, while the spectral dimension presents non-stationary and non-linear irregular coupling characteristics driven by the physical responses of ground objects. Such homogeneous feature extraction approaches lead to mutual interference between spatial structures and spectral correlations during modeling. This, in turn, results in limitations such as spatial blur and spectral drift in the reconstructed outcomes, as well as insufficient generalization and adaptability in continuous scale mapping. To alleviate the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes an arbitrary-scale SR network named DCMArb (Decoupled-Collaborative Mamba for Arbitrary-scale Super-resolution), based on a decoupled-collaborative-reconstruction paradigm. In specific implementation, this method tightly integrates physical mechanism analysis with network module design. First, the multi-dimensional dependency extraction stage (MDES) is proposed as the decoupling unit. It separates spatial long-range dependencies and spectral non-linear correlations through differentiated modeling to avoid the mutual interference between heterogeneous features, establishing a pure feature representation foundation. Next, the heterogeneous feature integration stage (HFIS) is designed as the collaborative unit. It introduces an adaptive mechanism to dynamically balance the decoupled pure features and filtered key details, thereby constructing a high-quality, interference-resistant spatial-spectral joint prior. Finally, the scale-aware meta-learned upsampler block (SMUB) is constructed as the reconstruction unit. Utilizing a mixture-of-experts mechanism, it maps this high-quality prior to a manifold function in the continuous scale space and performs high-fidelity arbitrary-scale (including non-integer) continuous reconstruction, thereby mitigating distortion issues in cross-scale transformations. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that DCMArb achieves competitive or superior performance compared with state-of-the-art single-scale and arbitrary-scale methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. Ablation studies and complexity analyses further validate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance and generalization with reduced computational costs. The source code will be made available at https://github.com/wangswhu/DCMArb.
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: WaveUNet: An efficient deep network based on discrete wavelet transform and attention mechanism for InSAR phase unwrapping
abstract: Phase unwrapping (PU) is a core yet challenging step in interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) measurements. Traditional PU methods rely on the assumption of phase continuity, which often fails in areas with steep topography, dense fringes, or severe decorrelation noise. While deep learning has emerged to address this limitation, existing networks suffer from two key drawbacks: (1) limited generalization due to training data that inadequately captures the complexity of real-world deformation, and (2) high computational costs caused by the use of deep architectures with extensive parameters and high-dimensional convolutions to pursue accuracy. These two factors lead to the insufficient generalization capability and considerable consumption of computing resources for these networks. To address these issues, this study presents a lightweight deep phase unwrapping network based on the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and attention mechanism, called WaveUNet. To train this network, we first simulate InSAR phase data to generate a sample dataset encompassing complex topographic and deformation features; subsequently, WaveUNet is trained by integrating the DWT and attention mechanism, achieving phase unwrapping with high precision and less computational resources; finally, we conduct tests on WaveUNet using the simulated dataset, the InSAR-DLPU dataset, and real InSAR data. The experimental results demonstrate that the GPU usage of WaveUNet is 32.96%, 24.43%, and 38.63% of that for VURNet, ResUNet, and PUNet, respectively. Meanwhile, its total number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) is merely 21.80%, 23.81%, and 9.23% of that for the three models, respectively. This illustrates that WaveUNet achieves comparable accuracy and efficiency to state-of-the-art PU models while utilizing limited computational resources. The related experimental code will be made available at https://github.com/xiangHQ/WaveUNet.git.
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: PRGD: Proximal Residual-Guided Diffusion with pattern-aware experts for remote sensing image super-resolution
abstract: High-resolution remote sensing imagery is essential for accurate Earth observation and analysis. While diffusion models show promise for image super-resolution (SR), their application to remote sensing is often hindered by fidelity loss from error accumulation and by inadequate guidance from simple low-resolution (LR) conditioning. To address these dual challenges, we introduce the Proximal Residual-Guided Diffusion (PRGD) model, a novel framework for high-fidelity remote sensing SR. PRGD is built upon a novel holistic paradigm designed to synergistically mitigate error accumulation throughout the diffusion process. This paradigm combines a Residual Shifting strategy, which simplifies the generation path by anchoring it to the LR image, with a measurement-consistent Proximal Sampling technique that enforces strict data fidelity at each iterative step. To provide superior guidance, PRGD introduces an innovative Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) feature extraction module, powered by our Pattern-Aware Deformable Convolution (PADC). This novel convolution dynamically groups feature channels based on their activation patterns to extract rich, adaptive, multi-scale priors. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that PRGD achieves a new state-of-the-art, establishing superior performance across both fidelity and perceptual quality. For instance, on the Toronto ×4 dataset, PRGD not only surpasses the leading regression-based method in PSNR but also reduces the Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) by 11.96% compared to the next-best diffusion model. The resulting images exhibit superior fidelity to the ground truth, enhanced visual realism, and remarkable detail preservation, thereby enhancing the potential of diffusion models to serve as a reliable data source for downstream remote sensing applications.

title: TALineNet: A benchmark and network for temporally-aware continuous line segment detection in event streams
abstract: Event cameras offer unique advantages for line segment detection in high-speed and high-dynamic-range scenarios, yet existing methods face two critical limitations. They primarily operate on isolated event frames, overlooking temporal continuity and unstable imaging within continuous streams. Furthermore, the lack of absolute intensity renders these methods highly susceptible to noise, hindering reliable spatial feature extraction. To bridge this gap, we first establish two novel benchmarks, Ev-WireframeSeq (synthetic) and Ev-LineSeq (real-world), providing the first sequential event-based line segment detection datasets with dense line annotations to facilitate temporal context learning. Supported by these benchmarks, we propose TALineNet, a temporally-aware network that delivers temporally consistent and spatially robust line segment detection from continuous event streams. The network leverages a recurrent backbone to capture long-range temporal dependencies and employs a background-line disentanglement (BLD) module to suppress noise and emphasize true edge structures. Moreover, a Bézier-based representation is adopted in the detection head to better accommodate the non-uniform spatial distributions in event data. To quantitatively assess detection stability over time, we introduce a set of sequence-level evaluation metrics, including the Geometric Stability Score (GSS) and Temporal Fidelity Index (TFI). Experimental results demonstrate that TALineNet achieves 57.7% msAP on the Ev-LineSeq dataset, outperforming the state-of-the-art by 12.9 percentage points. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/Qiuben/TALineNet.
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: Fusion of hyperspectral and multisource remote sensing data using intelligent optimized ensemble learning to estimate the SOC content of seven mangrove species in China
abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) in mangrove ecosystems represents a vital blue carbon resource; however, accurate characterization of its spatial heterogeneity remains challenging. Traditional approaches treat mangroves as homogeneous entities, which overlooks variations in carbon sequestration capacity among species and severely limits precise assessments of carbon sink functionality. To address this issue, this study pioneers the integration of multiple intelligent optimization algorithms with an ensemble learning regression model (PSO-ELR), fusing hyperspectral data simulated by the PROSPECT-PRO and 4-SCALE models with multisource satellite data (Gao Fen (GF), Sentinel-2 (S2), and Sentinel-1 (S1)), providing an indirect physical link between canopy remote sensing data and subsurface SOC, thereby enabling high-precision estimates of SOC content for seven typical mangrove species in China. The study revealed that different mangrove species exhibit unique spectral responses at the leaf scale, with the red edge, near-infrared, and shortwave infrared bands being the most sensitive for estimating SOC. Additionally, compared with genetic algorithm optimization (GAO) and the grid search method (GSM), the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm significantly outperforms the other algorithms. The PSO-ELR model exhibits the highest SOC estimation accuracy (R2 = 0.873–0.925) across the various datasets and demonstrated robust generalizability. Finally, the results of this study confirmed that mangrove species identity is the primary driver of spatial variation in SOC, with Bruguiera gymnorrhiza (BG) and Aegiceras corniculatum (AC) being the mangrove species with the highest carbon density (301.46 and 300.29 Mg/ha, respectively). This study recommends prioritizing the conservation and planting of existing high-carbon-density species (BG and AC) and optimizing the maintenance of widespread pioneer species such as Avicennia marina (AM) and Kandelia candel (KC) to achieve precise protection of mangrove ecosystems and maximize carbon sink benefits in restoration practices.
keywords: Smart optimization ensemble learning regression algorithm

title: SMS-Diff: Physics-aware spectral-spatial diffusion for unified geospatial multi-modal reconstruction
abstract: In recent years, unified generative models have achieved unprecedented success in photorealistic synthesis. However, since satellite imagery serves as strict physical measurements, the geospatial domain requires capturing the complex multi-modal symbiosis across diverse sensors to achieve rigorous structural and spectral fidelity rather than mere visual realism. Currently, constrained by multi-modal data scarcity and inherent modality barriers, existing studies often fail to reconstruct underlying physical interactions and remain restricted to superficial perceptual synthesis. To address these challenges, we present the MMG-5 dataset and the unified SMS-Diff model. MMG-5 is a globally sampled, strictly aligned benchmark integrating five geospatial modalities (LULC, RGB, SWIR, SAR, DEM) to bridge the multi-modal data gap. Building on MMG-5, SMS-Diff transforms geospatial image translation into true multi-modal physics-aware reconstruction. Specifically, SMS-Diff incorporates a Spectral Manifold Injector (SMI) and a Latent Physics Resonance Loss (LPRL) to explicitly decouple spectral laws from spatial geometry, successfully bridging global frequency alignment and local structural precision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SMS-Diff achieves consistent improvements over strong baselines, achieving an SSIM of 0.315 and LPIPS of 0.307. Beyond generic computer vision metrics, we integrate classic geospatial physical indicators with downstream task utility as the dual benchmark for validating geospatial consistency. Crucially, these task-specific evaluations reveal a significant “Denoising Effect Tendency” in synthesized features, yielding partial accuracy inversions over raw sensor data. The model shows zero-shot transfer ability for change detection to some extent, while also scaling to reconstruction across 10 diverse modalities and multiple downstream tasks via low-resource fine-tuning. In summary, SMS-Diff drives a paradigm shift toward internally consistent physics-aware reconstruction, proving the feasibility of generative models to simulate the real physical world.
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: Segmentation-guided and attention-enhanced GAN for SAR image restoration under multi-type interference
abstract: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems are often affected by co-frequency interference, which significantly degrades imaging quality and subsequent image interpretation performance. Existing suppression methods typically focus on a single interference type or salient interference, which limits their effectiveness when confronted with multi-type real-measured interference. To address these challenges, this paper reformulates the multi-type interference suppression problem as a pre-imaging clean SAR echo restoration task, and proposes a novel SC2-GAN framework for SAR imaging. Built upon a generative adversarial network, SC2-GAN integrates three synergistic components: segmentation-guided mechanism (SGM), convolutional block attention module (CBAM), and conditionally parameterized convolution module (CondConv). The SGM extracts the spatial location and type information of interference in shallow feature space, enabling differentiated attention to multiple interference types. CBAM captures discriminative features in both channel and spatial through dual attention mechanisms, enhancing the network’s ability to perceive interference features in deeper layers. CondConv adaptively generates convolutional kernels according to input features, enabling the network to respond differently to diverse interference intensities and patterns in the parameter space. The synergy of these components forms the foundation of SC2-GAN’s adaptability to multi-type and multi-intensity interference. In addition, SC2-GAN achieves accurate interference suppression and segmentation in an end-to-end manner using a shared network architecture. Experiments conducted on seven simulated datasets and ten real-measured Sentinel-1 datasets demonstrate that the proposed SC2-GAN can suppress multiple types of interference and improved SAR imaging quality. The source code and datasets are publicly available at: https://github.com/XIAOYU-XU2805/SC2-GAN.

title: PELNet: A general physics-embedded learning framework for polarimetric target decomposition
abstract: Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) provides full polarimetric measurements, from which physically meaningful scattering parameters can be derived through target decomposition. Traditional model-driven methods often suffer from rigid power allocation, sensitivity to noise, and limited capability in representing complex scattering scenes. In contrast, deep learning-based approaches can learn intricate scattering patterns directly from data with greater flexibility. Nevertheless, these purely data-driven methods usually model scattering mechanisms as black boxes, resulting in limited physical interpretability and reduced generalization to complex or unseen scenarios. Building on these observations, we investigate the integration of physical priors into deep neural networks and propose PELNet, a physics-embedded end-to-end framework for polarimetric target decomposition. The core innovation of PELNet lies in structurally embedding a differentiable scattering model within the network decoder, establishing a strict correspondence between the latent space and interpretable physical parameters. Specifically, a multi-scale SE-attention encoder is used to extract context-aware polarimetric features, while a lightweight Mixture-of-Experts module enables adaptive modeling of different volume scattering components. Furthermore, a differentiable scattering reconstruction layer embeds the physical scattering model directly into the network decoder, establishing an interpretable mapping between latent representations and physical parameters. A physically guided loss function is further introduced to enhance reconstruction fidelity and spatial consistency. Experiments on multi-band PolSAR datasets across diverse terrain types demonstrate that PELNet achieves superior accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional methods, providing a new perspective for PolSAR image interpretation and physical parameter inversion. The source code and pretrained models are publicly available at https://github.com/shurongz/PhyDecomp.
journal_title: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing

title: SAF-CropNet: Spatially adaptive fusion of SAR and optical imagery for semantic segmentation in operational cropland mapping across regions
abstract: Accurate cropland mapping from remote sensing imagery is essential for agricultural monitoring, food security assessment, and land resource management. Although optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) observations provide complementary information for cropland extraction, their local contributions vary across imaging conditions, land-cover backgrounds, parcel morphologies, and regional agricultural systems. This variability limits direct concatenation and static fusion, as modality-specific errors may propagate into segmentation outputs in the absence of spatially adaptive weighting. This study proposes SAF-CropNet, a spatially adaptive SAR–optical fusion framework for binary cropland semantic segmentation. Specifically, SAF-CropNet first extracts modality-specific SAR structural features and optical spectral-textural features through separate encoder branches. The Paired Reciprocal Inter-modal Selective Modulator enhances complementary SAR–optical interactions, while the Contextual State-space Modeling module captures long-range parcel organization. A spatially adaptive fusion head then estimates per-pixel contribution weights for SAR, optical, and contextual features before decoding. Evaluation was conducted on a seven-area SAR–optical benchmark spanning China, Germany, and France. The benchmark integrates GF1/GF3 and Sentinel-1/2 imagery with reference labels derived from field surveys and RapidCrops products and covers fragmented smallholder systems, water-rich and peri-urban mosaics, and large mechanized cropland. Within-region five-fold validation shows that SAF-CropNet achieves an average F1 score of 0.8550 and an mIoU of 0.8068, outperforming the evaluated segmentation baselines while remaining lightweight, with 3.38 M parameters and 6.21 GFLOPs for 256 × 256 SAR–optical inputs. In leave-one-area-out transfer experiments, stratified few-shot adaptation increased the average F1 score from 0.4986 under zero-shot transfer to 0.7698. Grouped cross-continental and cross-sensor experiments further showed that direct transfer remains constrained under compound shifts in sensor characteristics, spatial resolution, landscape structure, and reference-label conventions. These findings indicate that SAF-CropNet combines strong within-region segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency with substantial gains from limited target-domain adaptation, while direct zero-shot generalization under severe compound domain shifts remains limited.

title: Nested generative downscaling of passive microwave satellite data for navigation-scale Arctic sea ice forecasting
abstract: Rapid Arctic sea ice decline is increasing the accessibility of high-latitude shipping routes, but route-scale planning remains limited by the spatial resolution and ice-edge accuracy of Arctic sea ice concentration (SIC) forecasts. Coarse forecast products can smooth marginal ice zones, narrow straits, and fine-scale ice-edge features that are important for identifying navigable corridors during seasonal melt and freeze-up. Here we introduce IceNest, a navigation-oriented Arctic SIC forecasting framework that generates daily 6.25 km SIC forecasts up to 30 days ahead. IceNest couples a deep learning-based 25 km pan-Arctic forecast ensemble with a conditional diffusion model for residual downscaling. The forecasting ensemble uses the long OSI SAF SSM/I(S) passive microwave record together with historical environmental variables from ERA5, while the downscaling model learns AMSR-scale residual corrections from AMSR-series observations. Across 2020–2023, IceNest outperformed damped persistence and the evaluated Copernicus Climate Change Service seasonal forecast systems in terms of binary accuracy and integrated ice-edge error, with the largest gains during summer melt and autumn freeze-up. Route simulations along the Northeast Passage further yielded smaller errors in navigable-window timing and route distance than GloSea5/6 when evaluated against an AMSR2-based reference, highlighting the framework’s relevance to Arctic transit planning.

title: PatchFusion: Resilient LiDAR-camera fusion for point cloud semantic segmentation in autonomous driving
abstract: LiDAR-camera fusion for point cloud semantic segmentation is essential for accurate and reliable 3D perception of autonomous driving systems. Contemporary LiDAR-camera fusion approaches predominantly integrate the pixel-level camera features located by projected points to augment the corresponding 3D points, which can be abstractly defined as point-pixel fusion strategy. Although such point-pixel fusion mode has been proved to be effective and widely used in practice, the strategy has two non-ignorable defects: (1) dependent on precise point-pixel projection correspondence, (2) limited by just using extremely little image information. Besides, the LiDAR-only inference in offline fusion fails to utilize the synchronously obtained images to achieve a dynamic fusion for 3D perception, while LiDAR-camera fusion inference in online fusion still encounters challenges of field of view (FoV) discrepancy between sensors. Moreover, the corruption robustness of LiDAR-camera fusion methods for 3D semantic segmentation, a crucial factor for the practical reliability of perception systems, has received limited attention. Thus, focusing on addressing above challenges, we develop the point-patch fusion mode, and construct PatchFusion framework as a systematic and promising solution to enhance performance and resilience of LiDAR-camera fusion perception in realistic and complex driving scenes. Specifically, in PatchFusion, we propose to leverage cross-attention mechanism to implement high-quality point-patch fusion by automatically searching what information should be highlighted or suppressed from the local patch of image, thereby alleviating the adverse effects of projection errors, maximizing the utilization of the high-density image information, and being more robust to the potential image corruptions. Besides, we integrate the strengths of offline and online fusion modes and propose a bidirectional cross-modality knowledge distillation strategy, aiming to further enhance the performance and robustness for predictions within and outside camera FoV. Finally, to bridge the research gap regarding the corruption robustness of LiDAR-camera fusion methods, we design a specialized dataset corruption suite for public multimodal datasets to simulate complex evaluation conditions by synthesizing projection noises and image corruptions. Extensive experiments on well-known datasets in autonomous driving (SemanticKITTI and nuScenes) demonstrate that PatchFusion can effectively improve the performance and resilience of LiDAR-camera fusion for 3D semantic segmentation on both clean and corrupted datasets. The relevant code will be available at https://github.com/sssssyf/PatchFusion.
